thread:
yara: Hi team, first day here. Running Arch Linux on a ThinkPad, using the company WireGuard split-tunnel profile. Trying to reach internal services (registry.internal.redwood and api.internal.redwood) and keep getting TLS cert mismatches — the host resolves to an IPv6 address and presents the public cert. IPv4 seems ok. Any ideas?

infra-jen: welcome! quick checks: `dig A registry.internal.redwood +short` and `dig AAAA registry.internal.redwood +short`, `ip -6 route`, and `wg show` (redact keys). Also `curl -v https://registry.internal.redwood/ --ipv4` vs default to see difference.

yara: pasted outputs:
```
$ dig A registry.internal.redwood +short
10.60.4.12

$ dig AAAA registry.internal.redwood +short
2001:db8:10:60::4

$ ip -6 route
::1 dev lo proto kernel metric 0 pref medium
fe80::/64 dev wlan0 proto kernel metric 256 pref medium
::/0 via fe80::1 dev wlan0 proto ra metric 1024 pref medium
# no route via wg0 for fd or 2001:db8 prefixes

$ wg show
interface: wg0
  inet: 10.60.45.9/24
  latest handshake: 1m
```
Curl behavior: default `curl -v https://registry.internal.redwood/` connects to 2001:db8:... and TLS cert is for `registry.redwood-public.com` so TLS mismatch. `curl -4 https://registry.internal.redwood/` returns registry API JSON fine.

netty: sounds like IPv6 leak — your resolver returns AAAA (internal) but WireGuard profile doesn't install IPv6 routes, so the system falls back to the public IPv6 path (our public LB advertises a global IPv6) and you hit the public cert. Two quick workarounds: 1) force IPv4 for now (`curl -4`, `GIT_SSH_COMMAND='ssh -4'`), or 2) add an IPv6 route for the internal prefix via wg0: `sudo ip -6 route add 2001:db8:10:60::/64 dev wg0` (replace prefix with the internal one).

yara: tried `sudo ip -6 route add 2001:db8:10:60::/64 dev wg0` and re-ran curl — now default resolves and connects to the internal IPv6 and TLS matches. Is it safe to add that route persistently?

infra-jen: good catch. short-term it's fine to add route manually, but we'll update the onboarding WireGuard config to push the internal IPv6 routes to clients (we intentionally omitted IPv6 from old profiles). For persistence, add to NetworkManager or your wg-quick config: under `[Interface]`/`PostUp` add the ip -6 route, or in wg config set `AllowedIPs = 10.60.0.0/16,2001:db8:10::/48` so the client knows to route those via wg. We'll open a ticket to fix profiles.

yara: note — `sysctl net.ipv6.conf.all.disable_ipv6=1` also makes things work (forces IPv4) but not ideal.

netty: adding: if you prefer not to touch IPv6 routes, another short-term trick is to prefer A lookups by using `curl https://registry.internal.redwood -4` and `git -c http.proxyattempts=1 clone ...` but yeah we'll push routes.

bastion-bot: Bastion SOCKS proxy available: `ssh -D 1080 yara@bastion.internal` (if you need a proxy path).

ops-bot: INF-1600 created: "ipv6 leakage with split-tunnel wg profiles - onboarding" assigned to eng-infra.

infra-jen: we'll update the WireGuard onboarding profile to include internal IPv6 prefixes or explicitly disable AAAA in the scoped DNS for new hires. Thanks for flagging this on day one.

yara: thanks all! adding a short note to the onboarding checklist: "If internal hosts present AAAA addresses and WG profile lacks IPv6 AllowedIPs, add per-link ipv6 routes or use -4 until profile updated." Saved me a few hours. :thumbsup:
